fields.reasoning: Intent: the evidence is a Nebari plan run (01M6VY5APJP9, PR #78) blocked by a Rails flake, and the closest precedent, the ci-triage RSpec fix (01M6TB6N, decision-ci-triage-runners), served m27-nebari-on-rhiza ('Nebari's daemon builds and ships a Nebari change set on its own with Rhiza's workflows'); a plan run that dies on an unrelated flake is the same blocker. Rerun: internal/api/ship.go shipRerunFailed stops after one rerun per head (st.RerunHead == resp.Commit && len(st.Reruns) > 0), and plan.toml's pr-green and rebased-green just run 'rhiza ship check', so the run fails on the second red; the question notes the first rerun already fired and failed and a third attempt passed, so the plan needs a second rerun per head, not the first. A budgeted flag on ship check keeps it deterministic, bounded and visible in the workflow file, leaves ship-change and ci-rerun-once-per-head unchanged by default, and avoids an agent step for a plan whose diff is only .rhiza/. Naming: ship check already parses failing tests from --log-failed (parseFailedTests, shipReadFailures), so reusing it names the test; the note says only that the diff is .rhiza-only, never that the failure is unrelated, because a repo whose CI reads .rhiza/ (Rhiza's make check runs self-check) can go red on a plan's own content, so the note stays true whichever workflow or repo calls it. Failing: the change set's intent says 'rerun the failed jobs once (budgeted) and only then fail', and merging on red would bypass the repo's required checks and could hide a real break on main; the reruns absorb ordinary flakes and a persistent red is worth the owner's eye, now with a message that names the failing tests and says the PR changes only .rhiza/.
fields.statement: Change set 01M6WHT serves intent m27-nebari-on-rhiza (01M6J303FW4PYT5E5CE39QNHJ8). (1) Rerun budget: rhiza ship check takes a --reruns <n> flag (default 1, today's ci-rerun-once-per-head behaviour; n >= 1) that reruns a head's failed Actions jobs up to n times per head, each rerun recorded in the ship record (a per-head count beside RerunHead/Reruns) before gh run rerun --failed is called, so a crash costs a missed rerun, never an extra one; plan.toml passes --reruns 2 to every ship check in wait-pr, pr-green, wait-rebased and rebased-green, giving a plan PR three CI attempts per head; ship-change keeps the default, since its red CI goes to ci-triage and ci-fix. No agent step and no change to max_visits. (2) Naming: when a check is still red, ship check keeps today's detail form ('failed: <checks>; failing tests: <tests>', the tests parsed from the failed runs' logs as it does for ci-triage) and the human line's 'PR #<n> at <short head>: ' prefix; when reruns were spent on the head it adds ' after <n> reruns' after the failed checks, and when the PR's diff from its merge base touches only .rhiza/ paths it appends that the PR changes only .rhiza/, a fact and not a claim about the cause (a check that reads .rhiza/, such as Rhiza's own self-check, can fail on the plan's content), for example: 'PR #78 at 18230d2: failed: test (4/5) after 2 reruns; failing tests: rspec ./spec/system/garden_location_spec.rb[1:1:11]; the PR changes only .rhiza/'. A head with no rerun spent and a diff touching other paths keep today's detail unchanged. (3) Yes: a .rhiza-only PR whose checks stay red after the reruns still fails the step and ends the run failed; Rhiza never merges past a red check. The run's inbox item carries that message, and the owner judges from it and the failing tests whether the plan is at fault; and the owner resumes with gh run rerun --failed and rhiza run resume --retry as today.

fields.acceptance: A Go test in internal/api with a fake gh and a git repo shows a red head after 2 reruns failing with the detail 'failed: test after 2 reruns; failing tests: <parsed test>; the PR changes only .rhiza/' when the branch's diff touches only .rhiza/ paths, and the same detail without the .rhiza/ note when it also touches a file outside .rhiza/; a .rhiza-only head whose failing check reads .rhiza/ (a check named lint whose log reports a rhiza check problem on .rhiza/rendered/) gets 'failed: lint after 2 reruns; the PR changes only .rhiza/' and no detail in any case contains 'unrelated', 'flaky' or 'on main'; the existing assertions pass unchanged, including internal/api/ship_test.go's human line 'PR #7 at abc1234: failed: test, ci/x' (no rerun spent) and the testscript ship-check-ci-test-findings's stdout 'failed: test' (lines 39 and 51); run with go test -trimpath ./internal/api/... and go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/ship-check-ci-test-findings' only
fields.statement: When a head's checks stay red, rhiza ship check's failure detail keeps today's form, 'failed: <checks>' then '; failing tests: <tests>' when it parsed any from the failed runs' logs (the human line already prefixes the PR and short head, 'PR #7 at abc1234: '), and extends it in two ways only: when one or more reruns were spent on the head it inserts ' after <n> reruns' right after the failed checks ('failed: test after 2 reruns; failing tests: ...'), and when the head's diff from its merge base with origin/main touches only paths under .rhiza/ it appends '; the PR changes only .rhiza/'. The note states only that fact and never claims the failure's cause: a check that reads .rhiza/ itself (Rhiza's own make check runs rhiza check and fails on stale .rhiza/rendered/ files) can go red on a .rhiza-only head because of the plan, so ship check never says a failure is unrelated to the plan or a flake on main. A head with no rerun spent (for example a check with no Actions run) gets no rerun count, and a diff touching any other path, or one that cannot be computed, gets no .rhiza/ note, so those details are byte-identical to today's

fields.acceptance: A Go test in internal/workflow loads the built-in plan workflow and asserts wait-pr, wait-rebased (until) and pr-green, rebased-green (run) each call rhiza ship check with --reruns 2, with their on.pass, on.fail and max_visits unchanged, and that ship-change's ship check steps carry no --reruns; a testscript plan-workflow-ci-flake with a fake gh whose check fails twice on the PR head and passes on the second rerun shows the plan run merging and closing out with two 'run rerun' calls in gh.log, and a case red after both reruns fails the run with a detail saying the PR changes only .rhiza/; plan-workflow-pr still passes; run with go test -trimpath ./internal/workflow/... and go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/plan-workflow' only
fields.statement: The built-in plan workflow passes --reruns 2 to rhiza ship check in wait-pr, pr-green, wait-rebased and rebased-green, so a plan PR head that goes red gets its failed Actions jobs rerun twice (three CI attempts) before the step fails and ends the run with ship check's failure detail (the failing tests, the reruns spent and, for a .rhiza-only diff, that the PR changes only .rhiza/); no step, route or max_visits changes, and ship-change keeps the default single rerun
